must_fix.title: Nested Dialogs open on the same render: focus, Escape and the Tab trap go to the outer (covered) dialog
must_fix.evidence: src/Dialog.tsx builds openDialogs and moves focus in useEffect, and child effects run before parent effects, so the outer dialog ends up as 'top'. Probe: render(<Dialog open onOpenChange={outer} title="Outer"><button>o</button><Dialog open onOpenChange={inner} title="Inner"><button>i</button></Dialog></Dialog>); then Escape -> output 'focused: o' and 'outer [[false]] inner []'. Contradicts the README: 'With stacked dialogs, the ones beneath ignore Escape and the Tab trap until the ones above close.' No test covers dialogs that open together.

nits: Tabs handles Alt/Ctrl+Arrow like plain arrows and calls preventDefault, which overrides browser back/forward (probe: Alt+ArrowRight selected 'b')
Tabs has no selection until useLayoutEffect runs, so server-rendered HTML has no selected tab, no tab stop and every panel hidden
Combobox opened with ArrowDown highlights the first enabled option, not the selected one
Combobox aria-controls points to a listbox that is not rendered while closed; the 'No results' role=status is mounted together with its text, so it may not be announced
Dialog's Escape handler ignores defaultPrevented and isComposing; aria-modal is not backed by making the background inert

report:
I'd hold the merge for one fix. `pnpm test` passes (94 tests in 3 files) and `pnpm typecheck` is clean. Most edge cases I tried behave as the issue and README describe. But stacked Dialogs break when they open at the same time. I ran one probe in a test file under `src/`, deleted it afterwards, and `git status` is back to exactly how I found it.

## Must fix

**Stacked dialogs that open together are ordered backwards.** In `src/Dialog.tsx`, the order of open dialogs comes from which `useEffect` push runs first (`openDialogs.push(dialog)`), and the focus-on-open code works the same way. React runs a child's effects before its parent's. So when a Dialog sits inside another Dialog and both are open on the first render, the inner one is pushed first and the outer one counts as "top". Focus also goes to the outer dialog last.

I ran this:

```tsx
render(<Dialog open onOpenChange={outer} title="Outer"><button>o</button>
  <Dialog open onOpenChange={inner} title="Inner"><button>i</button></Dialog></Dialog>);
console.log("focused:", document.activeElement?.textContent);
await userEvent.keyboard("{Escape}");
```

Output:

```
focused: o
outer [ [ false ] ]   inner []
```

- **Focus:** it lands in the covered outer dialog, not the inner one on top.
- **Escape:** it closes the outer dialog, which also unmounts the inner one, instead of closing just the top dialog.
- **Tab trap:** it is also held by the outer dialog. The inner dialog is portaled to `document.body`, so its controls are not inside the outer one and can't be reached by Tab.

This contradicts the README ("With stacked dialogs, the ones beneath ignore Escape and the Tab trap until the ones above close"). None of the stacking tests mount two dialogs open at the same time.

## Nits

- **Tabs ignores modifier keys.** Alt+ArrowLeft/Right is treated as a plain arrow: `preventDefault()` is called and the tab changes (probe: `after alt+right B [['b']]`), so it overrides the browser's Back/Forward shortcut.
- **Tabs has no selection on its first render.** It is only set afterwards in `useLayoutEffect`. In server-rendered HTML, no tab is selected, nothing is in the tab order, and every panel is `hidden` until the page hydrates.
- **Combobox highlights the first option, not the selected one.** Opening it with ArrowDown while it already has a value highlights the first enabled option (probe: `active on open: Apple` with `value="c"`).
- **Combobox's `aria-controls` points at a listbox that isn't there while the list is closed.** Also, the "No results" live region (`role="status"`) is inserted together with its text, which screen readers often don't announce.
- **Dialog's Escape handler doesn't check much.** It skips `event.defaultPrevented` and `isComposing`, so inner widgets other than Combobox, or text input in progress through an input method editor (IME), can't stop Escape from closing the dialog. Also, `aria-modal` isn't backed by making the page behind inert, so mouse focus can still leave the dialog.
